questions.question: C2 holds a 15-character GSTIN. The PAN starts at the 3rd character and is 10 characters long. Which formula returns the PAN?

answerOptions.rationale: Starting at 2 picks up part of the state code.
MID starts at position 3 and takes 10 characters.
This includes the two-digit state code at the start.
This takes the last 10 characters, which end with the Z and check character.

questions.question: Remarks contain 'urgent', 'URGENT' or 'Urgent'. Which formula flags all of them as TRUE?

answerOptions.rationale: SEARCH ignores case, and ISNUMBER turns its position into TRUE.
FIND is case-sensitive, so it misses URGENT and Urgent.
This returns a position or an error, not TRUE or FALSE.
This removes the word; it does not flag the row.

questions.question: Names copied from a website still have gaps after =TRIM(A2). What is the likely cause and fix?

answerOptions.rationale: PROPER only changes capitals; it removes no characters.
Case has nothing to do with the gaps.

answerOptions.text: Too many spaces for TRIM; apply TRIM twice
answerOptions.rationale: A second TRIM still ignores CHAR(160).
TRIM removes only normal spaces, so convert CHAR(160) to a normal space first.

questions.question: House, Street, Area and City are in B2:E2, and some rows have no Area. Which formula joins them with ", " and skips the blank?

answerOptions.rationale: FALSE keeps blanks, giving a double comma.
The ampersand joins blanks too, leaving two commas together.
TRUE tells TEXTJOIN to ignore empty cells.
CONCAT adds no separator, so the parts run together.

questions.question: =A2&" joined on "&B2 shows 'Ravi joined on 45397'. How do you show the date properly?

answerOptions.rationale: B2 is already a date; joining still uses the underlying number.

answerOptions.text: Use VALUE(B2) in place of B2
answerOptions.rationale: VALUE turns text into a number, the opposite of what you need.

answerOptions.text: Format the result cell as a date
answerOptions.rationale: The result is text, so a date format does not change it.

answerOptions.text: Use TEXT(B2,"dd-mmm-yyyy") in place of B2
answerOptions.rationale: Joining shows a date's serial number; TEXT applies a date format inside the sentence.

questions.question: A2 holds 'Mohammed Irfan Shaikh'. Which formula returns only the surname?

answerOptions.rationale: This splits at the first space and returns 'Irfan Shaikh'.
This returns the first name, Mohammed.
An instance of -1 means after the last space.
This spills all three parts across three cells.

questions.question: Phone numbers contain spaces, dashes, brackets and +. Which formula keeps only the digits?

answerOptions.rationale: [^0-9] matches any character that is not a digit, and replaces it with nothing.
This removes the digits and keeps everything else.
REGEXTEST only returns TRUE or FALSE.
This removes spaces only; dashes, brackets and + stay.

questions.question: You split a bank export with Text to Columns on a Mac set to US dates. How do you make 02/04/2026 read as 2 April 2026?

answerOptions.rationale: Fixed width changes how fields are split, not how dates are read.

answerOptions.text: In step 3 of the wizard, set the date column to Date: DMY
answerOptions.rationale: DMY tells Excel the text is day first, so dates come in correctly.

answerOptions.text: Tick Tab as the separator in step 2
answerOptions.rationale: The export is comma-separated, and the separator does not set date order.
Remove Duplicates deletes repeated rows; it does not fix dates.
